_note: Curated companion to gen-contracts.mjs. Holds only the facts that are NOT statically derivable from web/src: event detail TYPES, gotchas, a11y notes, canonical examples, `since` versions, and token roles. Mechanical facts (attributes, event names, methods, slots, consumed CSS vars, API signatures) are extracted from source and must not be duplicated here.

druid-popover.summary: Anchored panel primitive: hangs arbitrary content off a trigger in the top layer, with light-dismiss and same-trigger toggle.

slots.trigger: The anchor element; clicking it toggles the panel.

css_vars.--df-accent: panel border color (override for a quiet-at-rest / accent-when-open trigger)

druid-popover.a11y: Panel is role=dialog; light-dismiss on outside-click and Esc (scroll never dismisses); same-trigger click toggles.
gotchas: placement splits on '-': base edge (top|bottom|left|right) + align (start|end). bottom-start aligns the panel's LEFT edge to the trigger; bottom-end aligns its RIGHT edge. Bare 'left'/'right' default to -start.
Panel is position:fixed in the top layer (native popover), so it escapes overflow/scroll clipping.
Tracks the trigger on scroll and resize (capture-phase scroll listener catches inner scroll containers too); it repositions rather than dismissing.

It aligns to the border-box of whatever you put in slot=trigger. A druid-button's inner <button> sizes to its content and won't fill a forced-wider host width, so give the trigger its natural size or the alignment will look offset.
Flips to the opposite side when short on viewport space, then clamps into the viewport.
Placement is druids.anchor(); use that directly to build an overlay control of your own that must escape a clipping ancestor.

druid-tooltip.summary: Themed hover/focus bubble that wraps the element it describes; works over disabled controls where native title is unreliable.

slots.default: The element being described (the hover/focus target).

druid-tooltip.a11y: Bubble is role=tooltip; shows on hover and focus-within, Esc hides it.
druid-tooltip.example:
<druid-tooltip text="Locked while a model is pinned">
  <druid-textarea disabled></druid-textarea>
</druid-tooltip>
gotchas: Empty or cleared `text` hides the bubble entirely — drive a conditional tooltip by setting/clearing `text` (or set `disabled`).
Bubble renders in the top layer, so scroll/overflow ancestors never clip it; it flips to stay on-screen.
Because the wrapper owns the hover, it fires over a disabled child control (unlike native title).

The top layer is the top layer of the tooltip's own document: inside a tiny iframe (a 40px extension toolbar) the bubble has nowhere to go and covers its neighbours. There, rely on the native title the control's `label` already sets — the browser draws that outside the frame.

attribute_notes.variant: soft / soft-danger added in 1.0.2; outline added in 1.0.3. outline = --df-select-bg background + --df-accent border.
attribute_notes.loading: shows a spinner and makes the control inert (clicks and submits are dropped); combine with your own request handling.

css_vars.--df-accent: primary fill, active/hover border, soft text

druid-button.a11y: aria-pressed reflects `active` when `toggle` is set; type=submit forwards to the closest light-DOM form.
gotchas: variant=outline is the dropdown-trigger look: --df-select-bg background with a --df-accent border at rest.
Recolor any variant with a df-ok / df-warn / df-danger class, which repoint --df-accent / --df-accent-soft.
The inner <button> sizes to its content; a forced width on the host does not stretch it.
loading does not disable the underlying button element — it suppresses the click in JS — so a form still sees the control, it just cannot be re-submitted.
druid-button.summary: Text button. variant covers primary, danger, outline, soft and soft-danger; toggle, loading and type=submit combine with any of them.

slots.default: Inline <svg> to render when `icon` is not set.

druid-icon-button.a11y: Set `label` for the aria-label; renders as an <a> when `href` is set.
druid-icon-button.example:
<druid-icon-button icon="pencil" label="Edit" toggle></druid-icon-button>
<druid-icon-button variant="soft" class="df-warn" icon="upload" label="Unload"></druid-icon-button>
gotchas: Prefer `icon="name"` (a registered icon) over slotting an <svg>; the icon must be registered first via druids.registerIcons.
soft / soft-danger mirror druid-button: colored wash at rest, border on hover; pair soft with a df-* class to retint.
loading does not disable the underlying button element — it suppresses the click in JS — so a form still sees the control, it just cannot be re-submitted.

The tone classes work here: `.df-ok` / `.df-warn` / `.df-danger` set --df-accent / --df-accent-soft, and every accent this component paints reads that pair first. They inherit, so the class on a wrapper tones what is inside it too.

attribute_notes.loading: shows a spinner and makes the control inert (clicks and submits are dropped); combine with your own request handling.

druid-icon-button.summary: Icon-only button. circle, small, toggle, soft, href and loading combine freely; set icon to a registered name or slot an inline <svg>.

slots.default: Light-DOM <option> children (read and watched; JS-populated selects work).

css_vars.--df-select-pad: trigger padding (default 6px 10px; df-shell-compact and [compact] tighten it)

druid-select.a11y: Trigger is aria-haspopup=listbox with aria-expanded (a button, or a role=combobox div with `multiple`); menu is role=listbox (aria-multiselectable with `multiple`), items role=option with aria-selected. Each pill is focusable and carries an aria-label with its position and the reorder keys; its × has an aria-label naming the value it removes.
druid-select.example:
<druid-select name="model" placeholder="Choose model">
  <option value="a">Model A</option>
  <option value="b">Model B</option>
</druid-select>

<!-- an ordered list of values, at least one, from a long list -->
<druid-select name="langs" multiple min="1" filter value="en,de" placeholder="Languages">
  <option value="en">English</option>
  <option value="de">German</option>
</druid-select>
gotchas: Set `name` to get a hidden light-DOM input so classic form POSTs carry the value.
Options are declared as <option> children, never rendered directly; they are watched via MutationObserver.

<druid-select> is not a labelable element, so a wrapping <label> associates with nothing (label.control is null). Use a <div class="df-field"> with a <span class="df-label">, and set label="…" on the select — it becomes the trigger's aria-label.

The menu renders in the top layer (native popover, placed by druids.anchor()), so an overflow:auto or overflow:hidden ancestor — a scrolling table, a .df-dialog, a .df-card — cannot clip it. It is display:none when closed, so it never inflates the scroll height of its container. Scrolling repositions the menu rather than closing it.

Narrow hosts: the select shrinks with its container and ellipsizes the label (130px is a floor only when there is room); the menu is capped at the viewport width and ellipsizes long options, with the full text in each row's title.
Keyboard: ArrowDown opens the closed select; while open, arrows move the highlight, Enter picks it, Esc / Tab close.

`multiple` keeps its state as a comma-separated `value`, so a picked value must not contain a comma (one is replaced with a space when committed). With `name` set, one hidden input per pick is written into light DOM, all under that name — the classic multi-valued field encoding.
`multiple` renders the trigger as a role=combobox div (not a button), because the pills' × buttons cannot nest inside one; Enter or Space opens it from the keyboard.

`multiple` is ordered: a new pick is appended, and the order is the consumer's to use — a `change` after a reorder carries the same values in a new order. A pill takes focus (Alt+ArrowLeft/Right moves it, Delete/Backspace removes it, both stopping at `min`) and is draggable onto another pill's place; the order settles during the drag and one `change` fires at its end. Sort `values` yourself if the app wants a canonical order instead.

attribute_notes.value: Also a live property: read `.value` for the current selection, assign it to select programmatically (no `change` fires for a programmatic set). A value matching no option shows the placeholder — unless `free` is set, which shows the raw value. With `multiple` it is the comma-separated list of picks (so value="a,b" is initial state); `.values` is the array view of the same state, readable and assignable.
attribute_notes.filter: Adds a filter box on top of the menu: case-insensitive match on label and value, prefix matches first, at most 100 rows rendered (a note counts the rest). Arrow keys move the highlight, Enter picks it.
attribute_notes.free: With `filter`: Enter commits the typed text even when it matches no option (an exact match is still picked as that option).
attribute_notes.multiple: Collects several values — an ordered list, not a set: `value` / `values` keep the picks in pick order, and a pill can be moved (dragged, or Alt+ArrowLeft/Right while it has focus) so an order can be built without re-picking. The picks show as removable pills in the trigger, the menu offers only what is not picked yet and stays open after a pick. `change` carries both `value` (comma-joined) and `values` (the array), including after a reorder. Pair it with `filter` for a long list.
attribute_notes.min: With `multiple`: the number of picks that cannot be removed (the pills' × disappears at the floor). Default 0.
attribute_notes.compact: Tight trigger (less padding, smaller chevron) for a crowded bar — the label gets the width back. It reflects, and sets --df-select-pad / --df-select-chev on the host; <body class="df-shell-compact"> sets the same two tokens for every select on the page.

parts.pill: one picked value, in pick order (only with `multiple`); focusable and draggable

druid-select.summary: Framework-styled dropdown over light-DOM <option> children, opening in the top layer. filter, free, compact and multiple extend it; multiple makes it an ordered list-of-picks control.

druid-tabs.a11y: Document-level tab strip; you own the .df-tab-panel[data-tab-panel] sections and toggle .active.
gotchas: The strip scrolls horizontally inside itself when the tabs do not fit, so it never widens the page on a narrow viewport — in the navbar or placed in content alike.
druid-tabs.example:
<druid-tabs active="home">
  <druid-tab panel="home">Home</druid-tab>
  <druid-tab panel="logs">Logs</druid-tab>
</druid-tabs>
<section class="df-tab-panel active" data-tab-panel="home">…</section>
druid-tabs.summary: The document-level tab strip. It only drives visibility — the panels are the app's own .df-tab-panel sections.

druid-subtabs.example:
Models
…
gotchas: Scoped to itself (unlike druid-tabs), so it nests inside a page tab.
Emits its own subtab-change plus a bubbling tab-change so visibility-aware children (druid-log-view) pause/resume.
druid-subtabs.summary: A self-contained sub-tab widget scoped to itself, so it nests inside a page tab; boxed merges its header and body into one card.

gotchas: Light-DOM input; fires `search` with the current value while typing, debounced by `debounce` ms.
druid-search.summary: Debounced search input; fires search while the user types, for live filtering.

druid-log-view.a11y: Self-polling log table; polls only while visible.
gotchas: src returns JSON: a bare array or {entries:[...]} of {time,level,source,message} or {raw}.
poll is in seconds (0 = off); boxed paints a raised header over a base-shade body (--df-panel-header-bg / --df-panel-body-bg).

A tone class (.df-warn / .df-danger) on the log view repaints the INFO level too, since INFO is the accent color — toned warn, INFO and WARNING read alike. Tone the panel only when that is acceptable.
druid-log-view.summary: Self-polling log table: fetches entries from src, filters by level, follows the tail, and polls only while it is visible.

druid-chat-message.example:
<druid-chat-message sender="assistant" label="llama3">
  Hi there
  <druid-icon-button slot="actions" circle small icon="copy" label="Copy"></druid-icon-button>
</druid-chat-message>
<druid-chat-message sender="assistant" streaming></druid-chat-message>
gotchas: User bubbles (sender=user) auto-tint slotted icon-buttons to the accent.
The actions row is sized for `small circle` icon-buttons; larger buttons overflow it.
Clear `streaming` when the turn is done — that is what reveals the actions.

The tone classes work here: `.df-ok` / `.df-warn` / `.df-danger` set --df-accent / --df-accent-soft, and every accent this component paints reads that pair first. They inherit, so the class on a wrapper tones what is inside it too.

attribute_notes.streaming: The reply is still arriving: shows <druid-dots> (look=classic while the bubble has no text yet, an inline smooth pulse once text has come in) and hides the actions slot until cleared.

druid-chat-message.summary: One chat bubble, sender="user" or "assistant", with an actions row and a streaming state that shows druid-dots until the reply arrives.

gotchas: Light DOM, so it posts in normal forms and autofills. maxlength -1 = no limit; autosize grows to content.
druid-textarea.summary: Textarea whose default height is set in line counts; autosize grows it to its content.

gotchas: The framework ships NO icons; register them once with druids.registerIcons({name: svg}). Unknown names render nothing.
Inherits currentColor and sizes in em; set `size` for a one-off.
druid-icon.summary: Renders an icon the app registered with druids.registerIcons(); the framework ships none of its own.

gotchas: indeterminate (boolean) animates an accent bar with no value.

The fill honours the tone classes — <druid-progress class="df-warn"> / "df-danger" is how a meter shows a threshold state. It paints var(--df-accent, var(--accent)), so setting --df-accent on any ancestor retints it as well.
druid-progress.summary: Thin progress bar with a value/max or an indeterminate state; a df-warn / df-danger class turns the fill into a threshold state.

druid-navbar.summary: The page's top bar: brand mark, the tab strip, and an actions region that also carries the theme, flavor and accent controls.

gotchas: No attributes; place in the navbar actions slot. Drives druids.applyAccent / rainbow.
druid-accent-picker.summary: Swatch menu for the app accent — the vivid hue. Belongs in the navbar actions slot; the pick is stored per app slug.

druid-footer.summary: The page's bottom bar: version line, author and repository link, rendered from the Druids object.

gotchas: Light-DOM, form-participating login form rendered by the framework login page; brand, action, error, subtitle.
druid-login-card.summary: The sign-in form, form-participating; rendered by the framework's own login page.

gotchas: A pill inside druid-tabs (panel + reflected active) or slot=tab inside druid-subtabs.

druid-tab.summary: One tab button, in a druid-tabs strip or a druid-subtabs header.

druid-table.summary: Sorting and live filtering for a plain light-DOM table (slotted, never rebuilt).

table-sort.key: string — the sorted column's data-key, else its header text

attribute_notes.sort: column key to sort by: a <th>'s data-key, else its trimmed header text.
attribute_notes.filter: the active query; set it from the app to filter without the built-in box.

css_vars.--df-panel-header-bg: header bar of the boxed table

druid-table.a11y: Sorted headers carry aria-sort=ascending|descending; the filter input is labelled from search-placeholder.
druid-table.example:
NameSizeActions
gemma8.1 GBrun
gotchas: The table is slotted light DOM: style it with .df-table and render its rows server-side as usual. The component only reorders <tr> nodes and toggles their hidden flag.
Sorting compares a cell's data-value when present, else its text; two values that both parse as numbers compare numerically. Use data-value for anything formatted ("8.1 GB", a date).
<th data-sort="none"> opts a column out of sorting (action columns).
Rows added or replaced later are picked up automatically by a MutationObserver; call refresh() only if you mutate rows in a way that does not touch the DOM.
Sticky headers and the scroll container come from .df-table / .df-table-wrap in druids.css, not from this component.

A .df-table is width:100%, so it can never outgrow the scroll container and a narrow viewport squeezes the columns. Add class "wide" to the table (or tune --df-table-min-width) to give it a width floor and get horizontal scrolling; tables with 5+ columns get that floor automatically under 720px.

The scroll container only engages if the table's ancestors can shrink: give any grid track minmax(0, ...) and any flex/grid item min-width: 0, otherwise the ancestor grows to the table's floor and the page gets the horizontal scrollbar instead. Applies to the automatic 5+-column floor too, which needs no opt-in.
No attributes; place in the navbar actions slot (the navbar renders one itself, left of the accent picker).
Flavor is the hue of the *neutral* surfaces, not the accent: it rewrites --flavor-hue / --flavor-on on :root, which moves every surface, line and text token (--bg-dim … --text-faint) together.
Swatch names are the accent palette's; the extra 'neutral' swatch sets --flavor-on to 0 for a pure grey base.
druid-flavor-picker.summary: Swatch menu for the surface flavor — the hue of the *neutral* surfaces. The same nine colors in the same order as the accent picker, ending on the same rainbow loop; the palette's default swatch is the default flavor.

druid-dots.summary: Three-dot waiting animation — "something is being produced" (a streaming reply, a model loading), where .df-spinner means "a request is in flight".

css_vars.--df-dots-on: the lit dot (classic) and every dot (smooth); defaults to --accent
css_vars.--df-dots-off: the resting dots in classic (smooth rests at a lower opacity instead); defaults to --border-strong

attribute_notes.variant: flash (one light runs left-right-back), fade (dots fade in turn), wave (dots hop in turn), pulse (each dot swells in turn). Empty picks one at random per instance.
attribute_notes.look: smooth: 6px dots, 28px wide, 1em tall — sits inline next to text and animates transform/opacity only, so it stays smooth while a stream repaints the page. classic: 10px dots, 50px wide, box-shadow animation — the larger, livelier one for an empty bubble.

druid-dots.a11y: role=status with aria-label="waiting". prefers-reduced-motion stops the animation and leaves resting dots.
gotchas: look=classic draws wave and pulse 20px above its own box and needs about 25px of room above the baseline — give it a block of its own, not a line of text.
druid-chat-message's `streaming` already places one; reach for the element directly only outside a bubble.

The tone classes work here: `.df-ok` / `.df-warn` / `.df-danger` set --df-accent / --df-accent-soft, and every accent this component paints reads that pair first. They inherit, so the class on a wrapper tones what is inside it too.

druid-theme-toggle.summary: One button cycling the theme preference auto → light → dark. auto follows the OS and is the default; the pick is stored per app slug.

confirm.summary: Promise-returning yes/no modal on the .df-dialog chrome. Resolves false on cancel or dismiss.
confirm.example: druids.confirm("Delete this model?", { danger: true }).then(ok => { if (ok) … });

prompt.summary: Promise-returning text-input modal. Resolves the string on OK, or null on cancel/dismiss.
prompt.example: druids.prompt("Pin as:", { value: current }).then(name => { if (name !== null) … });

form.summary: Promise-returning multi-field dialog — prompt() for more than one input. Resolves an object keyed by field `name` (number fields resolve numbers, or null when left blank; checkboxes booleans; everything else strings), or null on cancel/dismiss. `required`, the control's own constraints (min/max/step, type=email/url) and a per-field `validate` returning a message hold the dialog open and tint the field.
gotchas: Field `type` picks the control: "select" renders a <druid-select> (pass `options`), "textarea" a <textarea>, "checkbox" a checkbox row, anything else an <input type=…>.
A field's `hint` is also its error slot: a validation message replaces it and .df-field.invalid tints both. A field without a hint gets one created on demand.
A blank `number` field resolves null, not 0 — "left blank" stays distinguishable from a typed zero. Mark it `required` if blank is not allowed.
min/max/step are enforced at submit via the control's constraint validation (the browser's message lands in the hint slot); `validate` runs only after they pass.
Enter submits from any single-line input; Esc and Cancel resolve null. Use modal() instead when the dialog needs arbitrary content rather than fields.
An empty `message` renders no body paragraph, so a title-only dialog carries no blank line.

modal.summary: Open a modal with arbitrary content on the .df-dialog chrome (backdrop / Esc / focus-trap); returns the <dialog>, already open.
modal.example: druids.modal({ title: "Repo quants", content: node, actions: [{ label: "Close" }] });

registerIcon.summary: Register one icon by name for <druid-icon> / icon=.

registerIcons.summary: Register a map of {name: svgString} for <druid-icon> / icon=.

applyAccent.summary: Set the app accent color (hex); persisted per app.

ACCENTS.summary: Array of preset accent hex values (the palette).

applyFlavor.summary: Tint the neutral surfaces with a palette hue, by swatch name. "neutral" (kept for older apps) returns to the default tint. Unknown names are ignored; stops a running flavor rainbow; this only paints — <druid-flavor-picker> also persists.

clearFlavor.summary: Drop the flavor overrides so the surfaces return to the default tint (--df-flavor-default-hue) — what picking neutral does, without touching storage.

FLAVORS.summary: Array of flavor hue names, in palette order (the accent swatch names). The default is the palette's default swatch, like the accent's.

anchor.summary: Place a panel against an anchor element: position:fixed, flips when short of room, clamped and width-capped to the viewport, follows the anchor on scroll/resize; a panel with the `popover` attribute is also lifted into the top layer. The primitive behind druid-popover and druid-select — use it for an overlay control of your own that must escape a .df-card (overflow: hidden) or a transformed ancestor. Returns { update(), release() }.

THEMES.summary: The three theme preferences, in the order <druid-theme-toggle> cycles them.

applyTheme.summary: Paint the page dark, light, or whichever the OS asks for ("auto", the default). Writes the resolved theme to <html data-theme> and re-applies the accent, which is tuned per theme. Only paints — <druid-theme-toggle> also persists.

currentTheme.summary: The theme preference as picked: "auto", "light" or "dark".

resolvedTheme.summary: The theme the page is painted in right now — "auto" already resolved to "light" or "dark".

startFlavorRainbow.summary: Start the flavor rainbow: the neutral surfaces walk slowly through the palette's hues — the flavor picker's last swatch. Only paints; the picker also persists.

stopFlavorRainbow.summary: Stop the flavor rainbow where it is; applyFlavor() and clearFlavor() stop it too.

surfaces.--df-flavor-default-hue: the surface hue an app opens with — the palette's default swatch (the build checks they match); what clearFlavor() returns to
surfaces.--flavor-hue: the live oklch hue of the neutral surfaces; starts at --df-flavor-default-hue and is overwritten by a flavor pick
surfaces.--flavor-on: flavor strength 0..1 — scales surface chroma; 0 is a pure grey base
surfaces.--bg-dim: input / table / log wells — the page colour, as on GitHub: the border draws a well
surfaces.--bg-header: header bar of a raised thing (card, panel, table head); equals the card in dark (the rule under it divides), a pale grey in light
surfaces.--bg-hover: hover-state fill (transient only, never a resting surface)
surfaces.--df-panel-header-bg: header bar override (.df-card, druid-log-view, druid-subtabs, druid-table)
surfaces.--df-zebra: the alternating wash on a .df-table.zebra row
surfaces.--df-navbar-bg: the global header bar: GitHub's inset — darker than the page in dark, the subtle grey in light

lines_text.--border-muted: dividers inside a box (table rows): --border at 70%, so the box outline stays the strongest line
lines_text.--border-strong: edges that must read as edges (table rules, sticky header underline)
lines_text.--df-code-bg: the chip behind inline code — a wash of --text-faint, visible on every rung

accent.--df-accent: component accent override (defaults to --accent; df-* classes repoint it)

shape.--df-table-min-width: width floor of a .df-table.wide, and of any table with 5+ columns under 720px, so the wrap scrolls horizontally instead of squeezing (defaults to 620px)
shape.--radius-sm: tighter radius for dense chrome (inputs, cells, chips)
shape.--df-main-pad: padding of the page's <main> (defaults to 30px 22px, 16px 12px under 720px); df-shell-compact sets it to 10px
shape.--df-main-max: max width of the page's <main> (defaults to 1100px); df-shell-compact sets none
shape.--df-card-shadow: the lift every .df-card casts on top of its border
shape.--df-scrim: the dimming behind a modal dialog

focus.--focus-ring: box-shadow halo applied on :focus-visible across light and shadow DOM
focus.--glow: the same halo as a resting glow for lit elements

motion.--df-ease: shared easing curve — quick out, unhurried settle
motion.--df-empty-mark: brand leaf as a CSS mask url, published by theme.ts for .df-empty

ladder.--df-l-dim: oklch lightness of the sunken-well rung — the per-theme scalar the ladder formula reads
ladder.--df-c-dim: oklch chroma of the sunken-well rung, before --flavor-on scales it
ladder.--df-l-bg: oklch lightness of the page rung — the per-theme scalar the ladder formula reads
ladder.--df-c-bg: oklch chroma of the page rung, before --flavor-on scales it
ladder.--df-l-raised: oklch lightness of the raised card/panel rung — the per-theme scalar the ladder formula reads
ladder.--df-c-raised: oklch chroma of the raised card/panel rung, before --flavor-on scales it
ladder.--df-l-header: oklch lightness of the header-bar rung — the per-theme scalar the ladder formula reads
ladder.--df-c-header: oklch chroma of the header-bar rung, before --flavor-on scales it
ladder.--df-l-hover: oklch lightness of the pointer-feedback rung — the per-theme scalar the ladder formula reads
ladder.--df-c-hover: oklch chroma of the pointer-feedback rung, before --flavor-on scales it
ladder.--df-l-border: oklch lightness of the default line — the per-theme scalar the ladder formula reads
ladder.--df-c-border: oklch chroma of the default line, before --flavor-on scales it
ladder.--df-l-border-strong: oklch lightness of the line that must read as an edge — the per-theme scalar the ladder formula reads
ladder.--df-c-border-strong: oklch chroma of the line that must read as an edge, before --flavor-on scales it
ladder.--df-l-text: oklch lightness of body text — the per-theme scalar the ladder formula reads
ladder.--df-c-text: oklch chroma of body text, before --flavor-on scales it
ladder.--df-l-text-muted: oklch lightness of secondary text — the per-theme scalar the ladder formula reads
ladder.--df-c-text-muted: oklch chroma of secondary text, before --flavor-on scales it
ladder.--df-l-text-faint: oklch lightness of watermarks and disabled glyphs — the per-theme scalar the ladder formula reads
ladder.--df-c-text-faint: oklch chroma of watermarks and disabled glyphs, before --flavor-on scales it
ladder.--df-l-nav: oklch lightness of the navbar rung (--df-navbar-bg) — the per-theme scalar the formula reads
ladder.--df-c-nav: oklch chroma of the navbar rung, before --flavor-on scales it

df-shell-fixed.summary: Keeps the fixed-height page shell at every width, instead of handing the page back to document flow below 900px.
df-shell-fixed.notes: For kiosk displays and panels that are never phone-shaped.

df-shell-compact.summary: Page-level density for a panel-width host (a browser side panel, a popup): 10px gutters, no max width, a tighter druid-select trigger.
df-shell-compact.notes: Density only — pair with df-shell-fixed for a side panel. Sets --df-main-pad / --df-main-max / --df-select-pad / --df-select-chev.

df-tab-panel.summary: A page-level tab content panel, shown when druid-tabs selects its data-tab-panel.

modifiers.scroll: the panel scrolls its own content

df-row.summary: Horizontal arrangement primitive; collapses to one column under 720px.

df-stack.summary: Vertical arrangement primitive; carries the framework's spacing.

modifiers.sticky: a rail that sizes to its content and rides the top of its grid column instead of becoming a second scroller

df-grid.summary: Auto-filling grid; collapses to one column under 720px.

df-toolbar.summary: A bar of controls above a panel or table.

df-spacer.summary: Flexible gap that pushes what follows to the far end of a row.

df-divider.summary: A rule between sections of a stack or row.

df-card.summary: Boxed panel: a header bar over a raised body, the same split every boxed component paints.

modifiers.fit: size to content but never past the tab, scrolling inside once it hits
modifiers.interactive: answer the pointer with an accent-lit edge

df-card-header.summary: The header bar of a card.

modifiers.section: a card titling a page section — larger, accent-lit
modifiers.quiet: a small tile that should not shout its label

modifiers.flush: no padding, so the card draws the frame around a table
modifiers.column: flex column that spaces its children like df-stack (gap-sm / gap-lg apply)

df-card-footer.summary: The footer bar of a card.

df-table.summary: The framework table. Wrap it in df-table-wrap for the sticky header's scroll container.

modifiers.wide: a width floor (--df-table-min-width, default 620px) so the table scrolls horizontally instead of squeezing

df-table.notes: th/td .num right-aligns numerics; tr.selected marks a row; a cell's data-value is what druid-table sorts on; <th data-sort="none"> opts a column out. Tables with 5+ columns get the width floor automatically under 720px.

df-table-wrap.summary: The scroll container a df-table's sticky header needs.
df-table-wrap.notes: Horizontal scroll only engages if the ancestors can shrink: give any grid track minmax(0, …) and any flex/grid item min-width: 0.

df-stat-number.summary: The figure in a metric tile.

df-empty.summary: Nothing-here panel; paints the brand leaf as a faint, slowly breathing accent watermark.

df-alert.summary: A message that stays on the page (druids.toast() is the transient one).
df-alert.notes: It is a row (icon + one text block): give it a single content child and nest multi-part content in a df-stack, or the parts lay out side by side.

df-spinner.summary: Busy state meaning a request is in flight (druid-dots means something is being produced).

df-skeleton.summary: Placeholder shimmer for content that has not arrived.

df-toast.summary: The transient notification druids.toast() builds; df-toast-stack is the container it stacks in.
df-toast.notes: Built by the JS API — apps do not normally write this markup.

df-animate-in.summary: Entrance animation for content swapped in.

df-animate-rise.summary: Entrance animation that also lifts the content into place.

df-field.summary: Wraps a label, a control and its hint or error.

modifiers.invalid: tint the control and the hint

df-field.notes: Use a <div class="df-field"> with a <span class="df-label"> when the control is a <druid-select>: it is not a labelable element, so a wrapping <label> associates with nothing.

df-hint.summary: Per-field help text under a control; doubles as the error line.

df-switch.summary: On a checkbox, renders it as a switch; it stays a native checkbox.

df-dialog.summary: The chrome for a native <dialog>, opened with showModal().
df-dialog.notes: druids.confirm() / prompt() / form() / modal() build on this — write it by hand only for a dialog they do not cover.

df-login-card.summary: The framework login page's card; df-login-body, df-login-brand, df-login-subtitle and df-login-submit are its parts.
df-login-card.notes: Rendered by the framework login page — apps do not normally write this markup.

df-ok.summary: Repoint a druid element's accent pair to the ok green.
df-ok.notes: Sets --df-accent / --df-accent-soft, which inherit — on a wrapper it tones every druid element inside.

df-warn.summary: Repoint a druid element's accent pair to the warn amber.
df-warn.notes: On a druid-log-view it also repaints the INFO level, which is otherwise the accent.

df-danger.summary: Repoint a druid element's accent pair to the danger red.
